塔波管笛主要由竹管或木材製成，通常採用蘆葦、柏木或其他當地易得的木材。管身內部結: The tabor pipe is mainly made of bamboo or wood, usually reed, cypress or another locally available wood. The inside of the tube is a simple structure with fingerholes for the player to control the pitch. Some tabor pipes have a reed fitted at the top to help the sound. The instrument is usually between 20 and 30 cm long and fairly narrow. The outside may carry simple carved marks or cord knots, and the whole design is light and easy to carry and to play outdoors.
塔波管笛又稱三孔管笛或加盧貝管，屬氣鳴樂器，以單手按三孔吹奏，另一手同時敲擊塔波: The tabor pipe, also called the three-hole pipe or galoubet, is an aerophone played with three holes stopped by one hand while the other hand strikes a tabor, a triangle or another percussion instrument. Its origin is unknown, but it existed by at least the twelfth century and was long popular in France, the Iberian Peninsula and Britain. The Basque country treats it as a mark of folk culture and uses it to accompany traditional dances; in Andalusia it is used at festivals, the May Cross festival, sword dances and pilgrimage processions.
塔波管笛常以單手吹奏，另一手同時敲擊塔波鼓、鈴、詩篇琴、弦鼓、骨板或三角鐵等打擊: The tabor pipe is usually played with one hand while the other strikes a percussion instrument such as a tabor, a bell, a psaltery, a string drum, bone clappers or a triangle. It is used on folk occasions in France, the Iberian Peninsula and Britain; in the Basque country it and the tabor accompany traditional dance groups, and it also appears in local teaching groups for pipe and tabor. In Andalusia it is used at celebrations, the May Cross festival, sword dances and pilgrimage processions; in the music of the El Rocío pilgrimage the same kind of pipe is called the pilgrimage flute, the pilgrimage pipe or a higher pilgrimage whistle.
塔波管笛起源不明，但至少可追溯至十二世紀。早期已在法國、伊比利半島與英國流行，至: The origin of the tabor pipe is unknown, but it can be traced back at least to the twelfth century. It was already popular in France, the Iberian Peninsula and Britain and is still in use. In the Basque country it has risen in standing over the past century, especially after the end of the Franco regime, becoming a mark of Basque identity and folk culture, and new pipe-and-drum schools have been set up all over the Basque country to accompany traditional dance groups. In Andalusia it is used at celebrations, the May Cross festival, sword dances and pilgrimage processions; in the El Rocío pilgrimage the same instrument has other names, such as the Rocío flute, the Rocío pipe or the Rocío whistle.
塔波管笛音色明亮尖銳，具有穿透力強的特質，能在戶外環保式演奏中清晰發聲。其音域較: The tabor pipe has a bright, sharp timbre with strong carrying power, and it sounds clearly when played outdoors. Its range is narrow, mostly in the middle and upper register, and its timbre tends to a bright, edgy quality rather than a warm softness. The instrument resonates through the air vibrating in a bamboo or wooden tube, and the simple inside gives it a plain, primitive quality. Beside the round warmth of the modern flute the tabor pipe sounds sharper and rougher; beside the ocarina its resonance is more direct, without the ocarina's warmth. The instrument is often paired with drums, its timbre sets off the rhythm clearly, and it was an important instrument of medieval folk music.
